Gupta Billions

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The explosive court documents filed by the finance minister last weekend lifts the lid on 72 suspicious transactions in the Gupta empire

Unique Selling Point:
We have the original interview with Nazeem Howa and an interview with Sipho Pityana

Summary:
When head of the NPA announced last week that he was charging the finance minister with Fraud on what appears to be flimsy evidence, he drew a line in the sand, set off a host of unintended consequences that are all coming to a head. In fact the events of October have been called a seminal moment in our politics. What happens next is anyones guess. With the finance minister openly defying the president and for the first time the deputy president, the chief whip and top ANC cadres have supported him, its open war. Will the ANC split.

Further information:
This week the guptas have denied the claims made in court papers by the finance minister, the banks have yet to decide whether they will reveal details of the suspicious payments and the country waits on tenterhooks for the next big move from the president.

Press Release:


The Gupta Billions
Early in 2016, it was revealed that the Hawks were investigating Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan. On Tuesday last week the NPA charged him with fraud. This catalysed a monumental support campaign by civil and political society opposed to so-called moves to hijack the National Treasury. In a strategic move Gordhan has this week exposed R6.8-billion worth of allegedly suspicious Gupta-linked transactions. Carte Blanche brings analysis to the fray.


Script:


Gupta Billions Final Script TX Sunday 23rd October 2016


Commentary One
Its dizzy days at State Capture Central wrote 702’s political analyst, Stephen Grootes earlier this week.

Stephen
If you try watch it all your head will spin off its neck, so in 10 days- On Tuesday we have had Pravin Gordhan charged with fraud, by Friday the revelation that he has gone to court and lodged these papers and we see revealed in front of us this R6.8 billion worth of suspicious transactions by the GUPTA family. Saturday night/ Sunday Cyril Ramaphosa- the first time a sitting deputy president in our history has issued a public statement of support for a finance minister facing a criminal charge. And suddenly by Tuesday it seems that Sean ABRAHAMS is suddenly trying to back track. The only prediction I can give you is that it is going to stay moving at this pace for quite some time

Commentary Two
South Africa stepped onto a political rollercoaster in December last year when President Zuma fired Nhanla Nene, replaced him with unknown Des Van Rooyen, and then was forced to appoint Pravin Gordhan to prevent an economic catastrophe.

Investigative journalist Sam Sole says almost immediately the president regretted his choice of Gordhan

Sam Sole
We had sources that told us after Des VR was removed the president was planning how he could get Des Van Rooyen back in that position

Commentary Three
In Feb just ahead of the Budget speech, with a ratings downgrade looming, the Hawks swooped on Pravin Gordhan who was trying to cut spending, remove Dudu Myeni from the SAA board and was cautious about the proposed nuclear procurement. At the time he made this impassioned plea in a public letter

Up sound Carte Blanche Feb 2016

Commentary Four
In March South Africans learnt how the Presidents friends the Gupta’s influenced cabinet appointments. Absa closed their account in December and in April the remaining banks followed suit and their auditors abandoned them. Treasury started to ask questions as South Africa drowned in corruption.

LINK
Few from within the ranks of the ANC were prepared to speak out until a loyal comrade decided at the funeral of his friend he could no longer remain silent


Commentary Five
Sipho Pityana is an ANC grandee – serving as a senior government official during Nelson Mandela’s presidency

Sipho Pityana
The Guptas are continually doing this because they have the president in their pocket/They are rich and their tentacles are so extensive as to paralyse government, if there is anything treasonous, it is this!

Commentary Six
His speech at ANC stalwart Makhenkesi Stofile funeral in August went viral

Sipho Pityana
I hate to tell you this. That if South Africans lose this round of battle in the contest between the forces of darkness and the forces of corruption, versus integrity and good governance this country will go down the tubes. This is our last stand.

Devi
Nobody would ever understand what its like to be part of a liberation movement that succeeded but then democracy happened, hard fought for and then you find yourself a couple of the years down the line having to take a stand to a large extent against the very liberation movement you were a part of …….so that decision to speak out

Pityana breaks down and cries…fade to black

Commentary Seven
The battle is taking its toll. Last week Pravin Gordhan stood firm, even as it appeared the president was using state institutions to undermine him and the NPA’s Sean Abrahams charged him with fraud.

UP sound NPA Sean Abrahams
I can assure you there has been no political interference in this matter

Commentary Eight
Four days later Pravin Gordhan fired HIS salvo in this explosive document. Amabhungane broke the story

Devi
What is the Finance minister asking for?
Sam
He is just asking the courts to rule that the Finance Minister cannot intervene between the relationship of banks and their clients, but in a sense that is just one of the things he is trying to achieve




Commentary nine
The court papers also drag 72 suspicious transactions, flagged by the banks to the Financial Intelligence Centre, into the spotlight. The Guptas say they welcome the chance to explain the total R6.8 Billion rand in question

Steven
R 6.8 billion rands worth, even in dollars is quite a lot of money. So what was it being used for? Where did it come from? Was it just being funneled there. We don’t know the answers to those questions. Up until now we haven’t had a right to ask them but we do now.

Commentary ten
The transactions only list a name and a sum, but amounts like almost a billion rand going through the loss making Shiva Uranium mine account have piqued journalists interest

Stephen
We are talking about a lot of money being moved and the FIC is not happy with the way it was moved, so the stakes here are incredibly high

Link BANK
Had the minister not gone to court the R6.8 billion in suspicious transactions would have remained a secret because legally the banks couldn’t reveal the details.

Commentary eleven
In June when I interviewed Oakbay CEO Nazeem Howa, he complained the banks never gave them a reason for closing their accounts. Ironically it was Howa himself who gave the game away when he read Standard Banks letter to us

Nazeem Howa up sound reads letter

Commentary eleven
Howa later admitted he regretted reading the letter and he never did give it to the finance minister who asked for it

Sam Sole
That is also the funny thing – he keeps promising the minister no I will show you my full file and then you will see, and the minister keeps saying I haven’t received your file, and then you guys did this interview which the minister brings up and ya I want to know more about that, and that was never forthcoming from Howa

Link
Legally, the finance minister couldn’t intervene and force the banks to reopen the Gupta accounts, but these documents make it very clear that that didn’t stop Nazeem Howa from constantly demanding that he should.



Commentary Twelve
This chain of letters between Pravin Gordhan and Howa reveals the enormous pressure brought to bear on the minister

Stephen
It seems to show contempt for the law, the finance minister says I am not legally allowed to do this and yet- why do you keep demanding. I mean you have to wonder if look at Temba Maseko, the former government spokesperson who said how he was treated by the Gupta family – that I am not going to do this and he kept being told: you must! you will! and you wonder if that is a strategy that has simply worked with other ministers in the past?! Just Pravin Gordhan said I am not going to do it!

Commentary Thirteen
At the financial Mail Editor Rob Rose suggests we may now understand just why the President has still not signed the FICA amendment bill
BTGB
Rob
Well the banks always had a duty under the previous money laundering laws to have a look at politically exposed people – this new act allows them to dig deeper to have a look at the recipient of the money – so before you say AJ GUPTA and to see who gets the money in the long run

Commentary thirteen
The bill passed by parliament has sat on the president’s desk for four months
Rob
Well you have a look at the papers that came out last week, the Gordhan court application where he details suspicious transactions, and clearly these are transactions that include those of his son, it includes his friends the Guptas, the president himself as the person who can sign this thing into law, there is a personal incentive for him not to do this

Commentary Fourteen
This week Oakbay CEO, Nazeem Howa resigned with immediate effect. The JSE is asking some tough questions of Oakbay, and has given them a deadline to explain 5- or 6 transactions that Oakbay itself is investigating. But the Gupta’s legal team has called the finance ministers claims undiluted nonsense

Steven
Undiluted nonsense plays well as a phrase but it doesn’t give anything substance. The Guptas didn’t want to explain these payments before – now they have to do it and that will make it very interesting

Commentary seventeen
Next month the finance minister goes to court to face his fraud charge. Sipho Pityana will be close at hand. He is rallying South Africans in a campaign to save South Africa



Sipho
We have coalesced a broad civil society to unite behind the SA flag - reclaiming our country, we are demanding that the president should step down, he is in breach of his oath of office, and that he is incompetent and he has no commitment to protect and defend the constitution of the country

Commentary eighteen
But like the finance minister this mining man is paying a price to take on the powers that be.

Sipho
I received a letter from Jimmy Manyi. He threatened the unleashing of the might of government, because of the stand I took.

Commentary
Mzwanele Manyi is the presidents ally.

Sipho Pityana
You are a chairman of a mining company. We are going to instruct Minister Zwane to go after your company. Well deputy minister Oliphant follows up and makes a public threat, oh by the way we want to have a meeting with you about health and safety. I will not be shut up. No one will take a hard won right for me to express myself freely.
Devi
They can make your life difficult
Sipho
Regardless of the consequences. We fought hard for this freedom its not tradeable.

Commentary Nineteen
At first the Guptas said they were delighted to finally clear their names, but a day later they demanded the finance minister withdraw his court action and pay costs. He declined. Today after a long period of silence the CEO’s of some of South Africa’s biggest companies made a public stand against corruption, as they rallied around the finance minister

THE END 11 33

PROMO ONE 10 seconds
More on the explosive court document lodged by finance minister Pravin Gordhan that reveals 72 suspicious transactions in the Gupta group of companies.










PROMO Two 15 seconds

Commentary
The finance ministers court application reveals R6.8 billion rands worth of Gupta company’s suspicious payments

Stephen Grootes
R 6.8 billion rands worth, even in dollars is quite a lot of money. So what was it being used for? Where did it come from?


PROMO three 15 seconds

Commentary
ANC grandee Sipho Pityana has taken a stand against state capture

Sipho Pityana
I will not be shut up, no one will take away a hard won right to express myself freely.
